chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Parker and Flip Phillips compared as colleagues
summary: Flip was Granz's favorite for being prompt and easy-going; Parker was unpredictable but never late for Machito's sessions.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Okay, and now Flip Phillips did something with him on there. Did they get along well?
Very well, because Flip Phillips is a gentleman and so Charlie Parker - Charlie Parker was one of the
finest persons you could meet in your life.

I know at that time, that Jazz at the Philharmonic was getting very strong and there were names like Illinois Jacquet, there was Lester Young, Gene Ammons, Flip Phillips, and there seemed to be a lot of rivalry then and I understand that some of them didn't even talk to each other. Did Parker and Flip Phillips talk to each other? Were they friendly?
Yeah, let me tell you. Flip Phillips was the favorite of Norman Granz because ahhh ....

No, because ahh Flip Phillips has a way, is a very easy-going person. He doesn't drink, he doesn't do anything. You say to Flip Phillips, I want to see you 6:00 o'clock, he would be 5:30 in the place, ready to start. The other people .......
What about Charlie Parker, was he prompt?
No, Charlie Parker was unpredictable. He was complicated, he had problems, mental problems or emotional problems, whatever you want to call it.
Did he ever show up late to some of the recording sessions?

Not in my recording. He was so enthusiastic because it was like a baby like you present a new toy, something that appeal to him and he would pay respect to that particular thing; and he respected us because we respected him, so you know, it was a complete understanding.
